title: argus repo configuration
description: Configuration schema for .argus/config.yml files. Keys are grouped by when they actually run: top-level (static/spawn facts, phase-independent), phases: (worker permission contexts only — allow/deny/skip per lifecycle phase, nothing else), and one region per argus operation, sibling to each other: ship: (argus-side actions after a verdict), rework: (the rework-loop's own restart budget and per-invocation round ceiling), and review: (the gate/review cluster the reviewer and deterministic gate consult). Workers launch under --permission-mode dontAsk (default-deny): allow/phases.<name>.allow are what supervisor.ResolvedAllowForPhase actually resolves into each worker's per-phase permission grant, on top of a code-guaranteed structural floor (read-only git, argus worker self-calls) and beneath a code-guaranteed, unremovable deny floor (git commit/push, argus ship/rework/review/supervise) no allow entry can re-grant. All keys are optional; a missing file is equivalent to a zero config, which degrades a worker to structural-floor-only, never wide open. A key's superseded flat/relocated form (e.g. top-level rework_budget, or the gate/review cluster under phases.awaiting_review) still parses as a deprecated alias resolving to the identical field — see internal/repoconfig/config.go, internal/repoconfig/yaml.go, and internal/supervisor/permissions.go.

base_branch.description: Base branch supervise/rebase/ship resolve worktrees and PRs against. Without this, argus falls back to its own default-branch detection.

worker_placement.description: Where a spawned worker's pane lands. Empty/unset behaves the same as "workspace".

launcher.description: Command started in each worker pane after cd into its worktree. Empty/unset falls back to argus's own default (claude --permission-mode dontAsk). An explicit --launcher flag on supervise still overrides this.

forge.description: Self-hosted forge API shape for a host outside argus's auto-detected allowlist (github.com, gitlab.com, codeberg.org). An explicit --forge flag on ship/supervise/worktree prune still overrides this. Empty/unset behaves like auto-detect, which still refuses any other unrecognized host.

status_page.description: Status page to point at when a forge request or push fails in a host-shaped way (see internal/svcstatus). Checked before svcstatus's built-in map, which only covers github.com/gitlab.com/codeberg.org — required for a self-hosted host to get any hint at all. An explicit --status-page-url flag on ship still overrides this.

worktree_dir.description: Where a spawned worker's worktree is created. Empty/unset defaults to <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<branch>. A relative value is joined under the repo root, so ".." points at a sibling-of-repo convention (<parent>/<branch>); an absolute value is used as-is. Changing this shifts the worktree's nesting depth relative to the original checkout — see worktree_bootstrap_command's own note if that command hardcodes a relative hop count back to it.

brief_note.description: Free-text note appended verbatim to every generated worker brief. Region: top-level — injected once, at spawn, for the worker's whole lifecycle. It is not phase-triggered.
examples: Add a focused test and keep make ci green.

worktree_bootstrap_command.description: Shell command run once, synchronously, in a freshly created worktree, right after `git worktree add` succeeds and before the worker's agent is spawned. A non-zero exit fails worktree creation. Use this to bootstrap gitignored per-developer local config (env files, local settings) that only exists in the original checkout. Empty/unset runs no extra command. It runs with cwd already at the resolved worktree_dir location, after `git worktree add` already succeeded there — it must never attempt to create or relocate the worktree itself (git will refuse, surfacing as a raw git error wrapped in this command's own failure message). A script that hardcodes a relative hop count back to the original checkout (e.g. `cp ../../.env .env`, assuming the default two-levels-deep layout) breaks if worktree_dir changes the nesting depth; prefer deriving the repo root at runtime (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) over a hardcoded hop count. (Renamed from worktree_setup_command, itself renamed from worktree_setup_cmd — both old names still work, see Config.Deprecated.)

owner_stale_after.description: How long a worktree's owner-lease heartbeat (see internal/ownership, .claude/argus/owner.json) may go quiet before a mismatched caller on rework/rebase/ship/worker answer proceeds (with a logged notice) instead of being refused. A Go duration string. Empty/unset falls back to the built-in default (30m). An explicit --owner-stale-after flag still overrides this.

rework_budget.description: Deprecated: relocated to rework.budget. Still accepted at the top level — argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read — but new configs should use rework.budget.

allow.description: Tool-permission patterns granted to every worker in every phase, on top of the code-guaranteed structural floor (read-only git, argus worker self-calls) — a static, phase-independent base list unioned with phases.<name>.allow's own per-phase addition for whichever phase a worker currently reports (see phases.working.allow below and supervisor.ResolvedAllowForPhase). An entry that could authorize a deny-floor command (git commit/push, argus ship/rework/review/supervise) is stripped after the union — it can never survive into a worker's actual resolved allow set, regardless of what this list says.

ship.description: Argus-side actions that run after a worker reaches done and a verdict is recorded, initiated by the operator — not a worker phase, so these keys get their own region instead of living under phases:.

verify_command.description: Controller-side gate command run before ship commits, in addition to argus's own built-in hook detection. Empty/unset runs no extra command. (Renamed from the top-level ship_verify_command, itself renamed from ship_lint — both old flat names still work as deprecated aliases, see Config.Deprecated.)

title_prefix_template.description: Required PR/commit title prefix, mechanically enforced by ship on whatever title it ends up using (worker-reported, forge-fetched, branch-derived, or --title), regardless of the worker's self-reported title. "{issue}" is replaced with --jira-issue's key if set, else "#<--issue>" if set, else empty. A title that already starts with the rendered prefix is left alone; otherwise the prefix is prepended. Empty/unset applies no enforcement. (Relocated from the top-level title_prefix_template, which still works as a deprecated alias.)

rework.description: Argus's own rework-loop operation config, sibling to ship:/review: rather than a top-level static fact or a worker phase — rework re-dispatches the same worker back through the existing phases with findings as its brief, so it needs no permission context of its own.

budget.description: Restart budget: total rework rounds a worktree may ever be dispatched for, across every separate `argus rework` invocation over its lifetime — distinct from max_rounds, which only bounds one invocation's own loop. Exceeding it records an unwaivable rework-budget-exceeded verdict instead of dispatching another round. 0 disables the budget; unset/null falls back to rework's own default. (Relocated from the top-level rework_budget, which still works as a deprecated alias.)

max_rounds.description: Give up and escalate after this many request-changes rounds within one `argus rework` invocation — distinct from budget, which bounds every invocation's rounds cumulatively over the worktree's lifetime. Unset/null falls back to the --max-rounds flag's own default. An explicit --max-rounds flag still overrides this.

review.description: The gate/review cluster: config for argus's own gate/review operation, sibling to ship:/rework: rather than smeared onto the worker-permission phases.awaiting_review block it used to live under. Fires once, on a worker reaching a terminal phase, before a verdict is recorded.

gate_verify_command.description: Shell command the gate runs in a worker's worktree once it reaches a terminal phase, before a verdict is recorded. This is also the general-purpose escape hatch for any repo-specific mechanical rule ReviewPolicy has no dedicated field for (max_diff_lines/proof_required_paths/always_review_paths are a closed set): express the rule as a script that exits non-zero on violation and its failure becomes an unwaivable escalation, no argus code change needed. Empty/unset skips this check. (Relocated from phases.awaiting_review.gate_verify_command, itself renamed from verify_command, itself relocated from the top-level gate_verify_command — all old forms still work as deprecated aliases.)

max_diff_lines.description: Review gate: diffs larger than this (insertions+deletions) escalate. 0 disables the ceiling; unset/null falls back to the gate's own default. (Relocated from phases.awaiting_review.max_diff_lines, itself relocated from the top-level max_diff_lines — both old forms still work as deprecated aliases.)

proof_required_paths.description: Path globs whose changes require real_world_proof in a worker's report before the review gate accepts it. Setting this key entirely replaces argus's own built-in default list rather than merging with it. (Relocated from phases.awaiting_review.proof_required_paths, itself relocated from the top-level proof_required_paths — both old forms still work as deprecated aliases.)

always_review_paths.description: Path globs that always escalate to human/reviewer attention regardless of diff size. Setting this key entirely replaces argus's own built-in default list rather than merging with it. The one exception is .argus/config.yml itself: it is always checked regardless of this list, since it governs next run's own gate policy and can't be allowed to silently drop out by omission. (Relocated from phases.awaiting_review.always_review_paths, itself relocated from the top-level always_review_paths — both old forms still work as deprecated aliases.)

review_note.description: Free-text note appended verbatim to the reviewer's prompt. (Relocated from phases.awaiting_review.review_note, itself relocated from the top-level review_note — both old forms still work as deprecated aliases.)
examples: Pay extra attention to internal/supervisor changes.

review_effort.description: Reasoning effort for --review. Without this, the review command's own default wins. (Relocated from phases.awaiting_review.review_effort, itself relocated from the top-level review_effort — both old forms still work as deprecated aliases.)

phases.description: Worker permission contexts only, one nested block per lifecycle phase (planning, working, self_test, awaiting_review, blocked): allow/deny/skip are live rules, checked continuously while a worker reports the given phase. No operation config lives here — the gate/review cluster's canonical home is review: (see the top-level review property). awaiting_review still also accepts the gate/review cluster's old keys (gate_verify_command, max_diff_lines, proof_required_paths, always_review_paths, review_note, review_effort) as a deprecated alias of review.*; placing one under any other phase is a load-time error naming the phase it belongs to.

^phase\\.(planning|working|self_test|awa.description: Deprecated dotted form of phases.<name>.skip — still accepted, argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read. Drops this repo's own phases.<name>.deny addition for the named phase. Never removes argus's own hardcoded floor (e.g. planning always denies git commit/push, regardless of this key).

Deprecated dotted form of phases.<name>.deny — still accepted, argus prints a one-line migration warning when it's read. Bash command prefixes denied live (via a PreToolUse hook) while a worker reports the named phase, added on top of argus's own hardcoded floor for that phase. A repo can only add restrictions this way, never remove the floor.

livePhaseBlock.description: Live allow/deny/skip rules for one worker-lifecycle phase, checked continuously while a worker reports that phase.

allow.description: Tool-permission patterns granted only while a worker reports this phase, on top of the top-level allow list and the code-guaranteed structural floor (see supervisor.ResolvedAllowForPhase) — the materialized-toolchain layer `argus init` writes from toolchain detection and the interactive setup co-builds with the operator, one phase at a time. An entry here that could authorize a deny-floor command (git commit/push, argus ship/rework/review/supervise) is stripped after the union regardless of which phase it's placed under; it can never survive into a worker's actual resolved allow set.

deny.description: Bash command prefixes denied live (via a PreToolUse hook) while a worker reports this phase, added on top of argus's own hardcoded floor for the phase. A repo can only add restrictions this way, never remove the floor.

skip.description: Drops this repo's own deny addition for this phase. Never removes argus's own hardcoded floor.

awaitingReviewPhaseBlock.description: The terminal awaiting_review phase's live allow/deny/skip rules. Also still accepts the gate/review cluster's old keys here as a deprecated alias of the top-level review: region (see the top-level review property) — new configs should use review.* instead of nesting the cluster under this worker permission phase.
